p2.original: According to the 2020 Census, 22% of the U.S. population was 60 years old or older, which means that more than 74 million people have reached an age when they will need increased medical care.
p2.zh: 根据2020年人口普查,22%的美国人口年龄在60岁或以上,这意味着超过7400万人已经达到需要增加医疗照顾的年龄.

p3.original: The baby boomer population, the group born between 1946 and 1964, is comprised of more than 71 million people who have already reached retirement age or will soon reach retirement. As this population grows older, they will be faced with common healthcare issues such as heart conditions, arthritis, and Alzheimer’s that may require hospitalization, long-term, or at-home nursing care. Aging baby boomers and advances in life-saving and life-extending technologies will increase the demand for healthcare and nursing. Additionally, the Affordable Care Act, which expands access to healthcare for millions of Americans, has further increased the demand.
p3.zh: 婴儿潮人口是1946年至1964年间出生的,由7 100多万人组成,他们已经达到退休年龄或即将退休。 随着人口老化,他们将面临常见的保健问题,如心脏病、关节炎和阿尔茨海默症,可能需要住院治疗、长期护理或家庭护理。婴幼儿老化和救生和救生技术的进步将增加对保健和护理的需求。 此外,扩大数百万美国人获得医疗保健机会的《负担得起的护理法》进一步增加了需求。

p4.original: These data tell us, as economists, that the market for healthcare professionals, and nurses in particular, will face several challenges. Our study of supply and demand will help us to analyze what might happen in the labor market for nursing and other healthcare professionals, as we will discuss in the second half of this case at the end of the chapter.
p4.zh: 这些数据告诉我们,作为经济学家,医疗专业人员,特别是护士的市场将面临若干挑战。 我们对供求的研究将有助于我们分析护理和其他保健专业人员在劳动力市场上可能发生的情况,我们将在本章结尾的下半部分讨论这个问题。

p10.original: The theories of supply and demand do not apply just to markets for goods. They apply to any market, even markets for things we may not think of as goods and services like labor and financial services. Labor markets are markets for employees or jobs. Financial services markets are markets for saving or borrowing.
p10.zh: 供求理论并不仅仅适用于商品市场。 它们适用于任何市场,甚至适用于我们可能不认为是诸如劳动力和金融服务之类的商品和服务的市场。劳动力市场是雇员或就业的市场。金融服务市场是储蓄或借贷的市场。

p11.original: When we think about demand and supply curves in goods and services markets, it is easy to picture the demanders and suppliers: businesses produce the products and households buy them. Who are the demanders and suppliers in labor and financial service markets? In labor markets job seekers (individuals) are the suppliers of labor, while firms and other employers who hire labor are the demanders for labor. In financial markets, any individual or firm who saves contributes to the supply of money, and any entity that borrows (person, firm, or government) contributes to the demand for money.
p11.zh: 当我们考虑商品和服务市场的需求和供应曲线时,很容易想象出需求者和供应商:企业生产产品,家庭购买产品。劳动力和金融服务市场的需求者和供应商是谁? 在劳动力市场,求职者(个人)是劳动力的提供者,而雇用劳动力的公司和其他雇主是劳动力的需求者。 在金融市场中,任何个人或公司如果储蓄,都有助于货币的供应,任何借贷实体(个人、公司或政府)都有助于货币需求。

p12.original: As a college student, you most likely participate in both labor and financial markets. Employment is a fact of life for most college students: According to the National Center for Educational Statistics, in 2018 43% of full-time college students and 81% of part-time college students were employed. Most college students are also heavily involved in financial markets, primarily as borrowers. As of the 2018–19 school year, 43% of full-time undergraduate students were receiving loan aid to help finance their education, and those loans averaged $7,300 per year. Many students also borrow for other expenses, like purchasing a car. As this chapter will illustrate, we can analyze labor markets and financial markets with the same tools we use to analyze demand and supply in the goods markets.
p12.zh: 作为大学生,你最有可能同时参与劳动力市场和金融市场。就业是大多数大学生的生活事实:据国家教育统计中心统计,2018年全日制大学生占43%,兼职大学生占81%. 大多数大学生也大量参与金融市场,主要是借款人。 截至2018-19学年,43%的全日制本科生接受贷款援助,以帮助其资助其教育,这些贷款平均每年7 300美元。 许多学生还借钱支付其他费用,如购买汽车. 如本章所述,我们可以使用我们用来分析商品市场供求的相同工具,分析劳动力市场和金融市场。

p13.original: Demand and Supply at Work in Labor Markets
p13.zh: 劳动力市场上的供求情况

p14.original: Markets for labor have demand and supply curves, just like markets for goods. The law of demand applies in labor markets this way: A higher salary or wage—that is, a higher price in the labor market—leads to a decrease in the quantity of labor demanded by employers, while a lower salary or wage leads to an increase in the quantity of labor demanded. The law of supply functions in labor markets, too: A higher price for labor leads to a higher quantity of labor supplied; a lower price leads to a lower quantity supplied.
p14.zh: 劳动力市场有供求曲线,就像商品市场一样。需求法以这种方式适用于劳动力市场:工资或工资的提高——即劳动力市场价格的提高——导致雇主要求的劳动力数量减少,而工资或工资的降低则导致要求的劳动力数量的增加。劳动力市场的供应功能法:劳动力价格的提高导致劳动力供应量的提高;价格的降低导致供应量的下降。

p40.original: The horizontal axis shows the quantity of nurses hired. In this example we measure labor by number of workers, but another common way to measure the quantity of labor is by the number of hours worked. The vertical axis shows the price for nurses’ labor—that is, how much they are paid. In the real world, this “price” would be total labor compensation: salary plus benefits. It is not obvious, but benefits are a significant part (as high as 30 percent) of labor compensation. In this example we measure the price of labor by salary on an annual basis, although in other cases we could measure the price of labor by monthly or weekly pay, or even the wage paid per hour. As the salary for nurses rises, the quantity demanded will fall. Some hospitals and nursing homes may reduce the number of nurses they hire, or they may lay off some of their existing nurses, rather than pay them higher salaries. Employers who face higher nurses’ salaries may also try to replace some nursing functions by investing in physical equipment, like computer monitoring and diagnostic systems to monitor patients, or by using lower-paid health care aides to reduce the number of nurses they need.
p40.zh: 横向轴线显示雇用护士的数量。 在这个例子中,我们用工人人数来衡量劳动力,但衡量劳动力数量的另一种常见方法是用工时数来衡量。纵向轴线显示护士的劳动力价格,即他们的工资多少。 在现实世界中,这种“价格”将是总的劳动补偿:工资加福利。这一点并不明显,但福利是劳动报酬的很大一部分(高达30%)。 在这个例子中,我们按年工资衡量劳动价格,但在其他情况下,我们可以按月或每周工资,甚至按每小时工资衡量劳动价格。 随着护士工资的上升,所需数量将下降。 一些医院和疗养院可能减少他们雇用的护士人数,或者他们可能解雇一些现有的护士,而不是付给他们更高的工资.面临较高护士工资的雇主也可能试图通过投资物理设备来取代一些护理功能,例如计算机监测和诊断系统来监测病人,或者利用低薪的保健助理人员来减少他们需要的护士人数.

p41.original: As the salary for nurses rises, the quantity supplied will rise. If nurses’ salaries in Minneapolis-St. Paul-Bloomington are higher than in other cities, more nurses will move to Minneapolis-St. Paul-Bloomington to find jobs, more people will be willing to train as nurses, and those currently trained as nurses will be more likely to pursue nursing as a full-time job. In other words, there will be more nurses looking for jobs in the area.
p41.zh: 随着护士工资的提高,供应的数量将增加。 如果护士的工资在明尼阿波利斯圣城。保罗-布卢明顿比其他城市要高,更多的护士会搬到明尼阿波利斯-圣.Paul-Bloomington寻找工作,更多的人愿意接受护士培训,而那些目前受过护士培训的人更有可能将护理作为全职工作来进行.换句话说,该地区将有更多的护士寻找工作。

p42.original: At equilibrium, the quantity supplied and the quantity demanded are equal. Thus, every employer who wants to hire a nurse at this equilibrium wage can find a willing worker, and every nurse who wants to work at this equilibrium salary can find a job. In , the supply curve (S) and demand curve (D) intersect at the equilibrium point (E). The equilibrium quantity of nurses in the Minneapolis-St. Paul-Bloomington area is 41,000, and the equilibrium salary is $85,000 per year. This example simplifies the nursing market by focusing on the “average” nurse. In reality, of course, the market for nurses actually comprises many smaller markets, like markets for nurses with varying degrees of experience and credentials. Many markets contain closely related products that differ in quality. For instance, even a simple product like gasoline comes in regular, premium, and super-premium, each with a different price. Even in such cases, discussing the average price of gasoline, like the average salary for nurses, can still be useful because it reflects what is happening in most of the submarkets.
p42.zh: 在均衡的情况下,供应的数量和要求的数量是相等的。 因此,每一个想雇用护士的雇主都可以找到一个愿意工作的工人,而每一个想按这种平衡工资工作的护士都可以找到工作。 在 .中,供应曲线(S)和需求曲线(D)在平衡点(E)相交.明尼阿波利斯圣城护士的均衡数量。保罗-布卢明顿地区为41,000美元,平衡工资为每年85,000美元. 这个例子简化了护理市场,把注意力集中在“平均”护士身上。 当然,在现实中,护士市场实际上包括许多较小的市场,如具有不同程度经验和资质的护士市场。 许多市场含有质量不同的密切相关的产品。 例如,即使是像汽油这样的简单产品也会定期出现,溢价和超高价,每种产品的价格都不同. 即使在这种情况下,讨论汽油的平均价格,如护士的平均工资,仍然有用,因为它反映了大多数次级市场正在发生的情况。

p43.original: When the price of labor is not at the equilibrium, economic incentives tend to move salaries toward the equilibrium. For example, if salaries for nurses in Minneapolis-St. Paul-Bloomington were above the equilibrium at $90,000 per year, then 45,000 people want to work as nurses, but employers want to hire only 40,000 nurses. At that above-equilibrium salary, excess supply or a surplus results. In a situation of excess supply in the labor market, with many applicants for every job opening, employers will have an incentive to offer lower wages than they otherwise would have. Nurses’ salary will move down toward equilibrium.
p43.zh: 当劳动力价格不达到平衡时,经济刺激往往使工资走向平衡。 例如,如果明尼阿波利斯-圣的护士的工资。Paul-Bloomington年薪9万美元高于平衡,然后有45,000人想做护士,但雇主只想雇用4万名护士.超过平衡工资、超额供应或盈余结果。 在劳动力市场供过于求的情况下,每个职位空缺都有许多申请人,雇主将受到奖励,提供的工资要低于他们本来会得到的工资。护士的工资将逐渐下降。

p44.original: In contrast, if the salary is below the equilibrium at, say, $70,000 per year, then a situation of excess demand or a shortage arises. In this case, employers encouraged by the relatively lower wage want to hire 52,000 nurses, but only 27,000 individuals want to work as nurses at that salary in Minneapolis-St. Paul-Bloomington. In response to the shortage, some employers will offer higher pay to attract the nurses. Other employers will have to match the higher pay to keep their own employees. The higher salaries will encourage more nurses to train or work in Minneapolis-St. Paul-Bloomington. Again, price and quantity in the labor market will move toward equilibrium.
p44.zh: 与此相反,如果年薪低于70 000美元的平衡,就会出现需求过剩或短缺的情况。 在这种情况下,受工资相对较低的雇主希望雇用52 000名护士,但只有27 000人想在明尼阿波利斯-圣德以这种工资从事护士工作。保罗-布卢明顿.为应对短缺,一些雇主将提供更高的工资,以吸引护士。 其他雇主必须支付较高的工资才能留住自己的雇员。工资的提高将鼓励更多的护士在明尼阿波利斯圣城接受培训或工作。保罗-布卢明顿. 同样,劳动力市场的价格和数量将走向平衡。

p46.original: The demand curve for labor shows the quantity of labor employers wish to hire at any given salary or wage rate, under the ceteris paribus assumption. A change in the wage or salary will result in a change in the quantity demanded of labor. If the wage rate increases, employers will want to hire fewer employees. The quantity of labor demanded will decrease, and there will be a movement upward along the demand curve. If the wages and salaries decrease, employers are more likely to hire a greater number of workers. The quantity of labor demanded will increase, resulting in a downward movement along the demand curve.
p46.zh: 劳动力需求曲线显示雇主希望按照任何特定工资或工资标准雇用多少人,这是根据certeris paribus的假设。工资或薪金的变动将导致劳动力需求量的改变。 如果工资率提高,雇主将希望雇用较少的雇员。所需劳动力数量将减少,需求曲线上行。 如果工资和薪水下降,雇主更有可能雇用更多的工人。所需劳动力数量将增加,导致需求曲线下行。

p47.original: Shifts in the demand curve for labor occur for many reasons. One key reason is that the demand for labor is based on the demand for the good or service that is produced. For example, the more new automobiles consumers demand, the greater the number of workers automakers will need to hire. Therefore the demand for labor is called a “derived demand.” Here are some examples of derived demand for labor:
p47.zh: 劳动力需求曲线的转变,是由于许多原因造成的。 一个关键的原因是,对劳动力的需求是基于对所生产的产品或服务的需求。 例如,新汽车消费者的需求越大,汽车制造商需要雇用的工人就越多。 因此,对劳动力的需求被称为“衍生需求 ” 。 以下是衍生劳动力需求的一些例子:

p48.original: The demand for chefs is dependent on the demand for restaurant meals.
p48.zh: 对厨师的需求取决于对餐厅餐食的需求.

p49.original: The demand for pharmacists is dependent on the demand for prescription drugs.
p49.zh: 对药剂师的需求取决于处方药的需求.

p50.original: The demand for attorneys is dependent on the demand for legal services.
p50.zh: 对律师的需求取决于对法律服务的需求。

p51.original: As the demand for the goods and services increases, the demand for labor will increase, or shift to the right, to meet employers’ production requirements. As the demand for the goods and services decreases, the demand for labor will decrease, or shift to the left.  shows that in addition to the derived demand for labor, demand can also increase or decrease (shift) in response to several factors.
p51.zh: 随着对商品和服务需求的增加,对劳动力的需求将增加,或转向右翼,以满足雇主的生产要求。 随着对商品和服务的需求减少,对劳动力的需求将减少,或转向左翼。 这表明,除了对劳动力的需求外,需求还可以因若干因素而增加或减少(转移)。

p56.original: When the demand for the good produced (output) increases, both the output price and profitability increase. As a result, producers demand more labor to ramp up production.
p56.zh: 当对良好产出(产出)的需求增加时,产出价格和利润率都会增加。 因此,生产者需要更多的劳动力来扩大生产.

p58.original: A well-trained and educated workforce causes an increase in the demand for that labor by employers. Increased levels of productivity within the workforce will cause the demand for labor to shift to the right. If the workforce is not well-trained or educated, employers will not hire from within that labor pool, since they will need to spend a significant amount of time and money training that workforce. Demand for such will shift to the left.
p58.zh: 受过良好培训并受过良好教育的劳动力队伍导致雇主对劳动力的需求增加。劳动力生产力水平的提高将导致对劳动力的需求转向右翼。 如果劳动力没有受过良好培训或教育,雇主就不会从该劳动力库中雇用员工,因为他们需要花费大量的时间和金钱来培训劳动力。 对此类需求将转向左边。

p60.original: Technology changes can act as either substitutes for or complements to labor. When technology acts as a substitute, it replaces the need for the number of workers an employer needs to hire. For example, word processing decreased the number of typists needed in the workplace. This shifted the demand curve for typists left. An increase in the availability of certain technologies may increase the demand for labor. Technology that acts as a complement to labor will increase the demand for certain types of labor, resulting in a rightward shift of the demand curve. For example, the increased use of word processing and other software has increased the demand for information technology professionals who can resolve software and hardware issues related to a firm’s network. More and better technology will increase demand for skilled workers who know how to use technology to enhance workplace productivity. Those workers who do not adapt to changes in technology will experience a decrease in demand.
p60.zh: 技术变革既可以替代劳动力,也可以补充劳动力。 当技术作为替代时,它取代了雇主需要雇用的工人数量。 例如,文字处理减少了工作场所所需的打字员人数。 这改变了打字员左侧的需求曲线.增加某些技术的可用性可能会增加对劳动力的需求。作为对劳动力的补充的技术将增加对某些类型劳动力的需求,导致需求曲线的向右转变。 例如,文字处理和其他软件的使用增加,增加了对能够解决与公司网络有关的软件和硬件问题的信息技术专业人员的需求。更多更好的技术将增加对熟练工人的需求,这些工人懂得如何利用技术提高工作场所的生产力。 那些不适应技术变化的工人将面临需求下降的情况。

p62.original: An increase in the number of companies producing a given product will increase the demand for labor resulting in a shift to the right. A decrease in the number of companies producing a given product will decrease the demand for labor resulting in a shift to the left.
p62.zh: 生产特定产品的公司数量的增加将增加对劳动力的需求,从而导致转向右翼。生产某种产品的公司数目的减少将减少对劳动力的需求,从而导致向左转移。

p64.original: Complying with government regulations can increase or decrease the demand for labor at any given wage. In the healthcare industry, government rules may require that nurses be hired to carry out certain medical procedures. This will increase the demand for nurses. Less-trained healthcare workers would be prohibited from carrying out these procedures, and the demand for these workers will shift to the left.
p64.zh: 遵守政府条例可以增加或减少任何特定工资的劳动力需求。 在保健行业,政府规则可能要求雇用护士进行某些医疗程序。 这将增加对护士的需求。培训较少的保健工作者将被禁止实施这些程序,对这些工作者的需求将转向左翼。

p65.original: Price and Availability of Other Inputs
p65.zh: 其他投入的价格和可得性

p66.original: Labor is not the only input into the production process. For example, a salesperson at a call center needs a telephone and a computer terminal to enter data and record sales. If prices of other inputs fall, production will become more profitable and suppliers will demand more labor to increase production.  This will cause a rightward shift in the demand curve for labor. The opposite is also true. Higher prices for other inputs lower demand for labor.
p66.zh: 劳动并不是生产过程的唯一投入。 例如,呼叫中心的销售员需要电话和计算机终端输入数据和记录销售情况. 如果其他投入物的价格下跌,生产将变得更加有利可图,供应商将要求更多的劳动力来增加生产. 这将造成劳动力需求曲线的向右转变。反之亦然. 其他投入物价格较高,劳动力需求较低。

p69.original: The supply of labor is upward-sloping and adheres to the law of supply: The higher the price, the greater the quantity supplied and the lower the price, the less quantity supplied. The supply curve models the tradeoff between supplying labor into the market or using time in leisure activities at every given price level. The higher the wage, the more labor is willing to work and forego leisure activities.  lists some of the factors that will cause the supply to increase or decrease.
p69.zh: 劳动力供应呈倾斜趋势,并遵守供应法:价格越高,供应量越多,供应量越少。供应曲线模拟了向市场提供劳动力或利用时间从事休闲活动在每一特定价格水平上的权衡。工资越高,劳动力就越愿意工作和放弃休闲活动。 列出了一些会导致供应增加或减少的因素。

p74.original: An increased number of workers will cause the supply curve to shift to the right. An increased number of workers can be due to several factors, such as immigration, increasing population, an aging population, and changing demographics. Policies that encourage immigration will increase the supply of labor, and vice versa. Population grows when birth rates exceed death rates. This eventually increases supply of labor when the former reach working age. Another example of changing demographics is more women working outside of the home, which increases the supply of labor.
p74.zh: 增加工人人数将使供应曲线转向右侧。工人人数增加可能是由于若干因素,如移民、人口增加、人口老化和人口变化。 鼓励移民的政策将增加劳动力的供应,反之亦然。 当出生率超过死亡率时,人口增长。 这最终会增加工人在达到工作年龄时的供给。人口结构变化的另一个例子是更多的妇女在家庭外工作,这增加了劳动力的供应。

p76.original: The more required education, the lower the supply. There is a lower supply of PhD mathematicians than of high school mathematics teachers; there is a lower supply of cardiologists than of primary care physicians; and there is a lower supply of physicians than of nurses.
p76.zh: 教育要求越高,供应就越少。博士数学家的供给低于高中数学教师;心科医生的供给低于初级保健医生;医生的供给低于护士.

p78.original: Government policies can also affect the supply of labor for jobs. Alternatively, the government may support rules that set high qualifications for certain jobs: academic training, certificates or licenses, or experience. When these qualifications are made tougher, the number of qualified workers will decrease at any given wage. On the other hand, the government may also subsidize training or even reduce the required level of qualifications. For example, government might offer subsidies for nursing schools or nursing students. Such provisions would shift the supply curve of nurses to the right. In addition, government policies that change the relative desirability of working versus not working also affect the labor supply. These include unemployment benefits, maternity leave, child care benefits, and welfare policy. For example, child care benefits may increase the labor supply of working mothers. Long term unemployment benefits may discourage job searching for unemployed workers. All these policies must therefore be carefully designed to minimize any negative labor supply effects.
p78.zh: 政府政策也可能影响就业劳动力的供应。 另外,政府可以支持为某些工作规定高资格的规则:学术培训、证书或执照、经验。 如果这些资格更加苛刻,合格工人的人数将按任何特定工资减少。 另一方面,政府也可以补贴培训,甚至降低所要求的资格水平。 例如,政府可以向护理学校或护理学生提供补贴。这些规定将使护士的供应曲线向右转变。 此外,改变工作与不工作的相对可取性的政府政策也影响到劳动力供应。其中包括失业津贴、产假、儿童保育津贴和福利政策。 例如,儿童保育津贴可能增加工作母亲的劳动力供应。长期失业福利可能阻碍失业工人寻找工作。 因此,所有这些政策都必须仔细设计,以尽量减少任何不利的劳动力供应影响。

p79.original: A change in salary will lead to a movement along labor demand or labor supply curves, but it will not shift those curves. However, other events like those we have outlined here will cause either the demand or the supply of labor to shift, and thus will move the labor market to a new equilibrium salary and quantity.
p79.zh: 工资的变动将导致沿着劳动力需求或劳动力供给曲线移动,但不会改变这些曲线。 然而,像我们在此概述的其他一些事件,将造成劳动力的需求或供应的转变,从而将劳动力市场转向新的平衡工资和数量。

p80.original: Technology and Wage Inequality: The Four-Step Process
p80.zh: 技术和工资不平等:四阶段进程

p81.original: Economic events can change the equilibrium salary (or wage) and quantity of labor. Consider how the wave of new information technologies, like computer and telecommunications networks, has affected low-skill and high-skill workers in the U.S. economy. From the perspective of employers who demand labor, these new technologies are often a substitute for low-skill laborers like file clerks who used to keep file cabinets full of paper records of transactions. However, the same new technologies are a complement to high-skill workers like managers, who benefit from the technological advances by having the ability to monitor more information, communicate more easily, and juggle a wider array of responsibilities. How will the new technologies affect the wages of high-skill and low-skill workers? For this question, the four-step process of analyzing how shifts in supply or demand affect a market (introduced in Demand and Supply) works in this way:
p81.zh: 经济事件可以改变平衡的工资(或工资)和劳动力数量。考虑一下计算机和电信网络等新信息技术的浪潮如何影响了美国经济中的低技能和高技能工人. 从需要劳动力的雇主的角度来看,这些新技术往往可以代替低技能的劳工,如档案员,他们以前把文件柜里装满了纸质的交易记录. 然而,同样的新技术是对管理人员等高技能工人的补充,他们能够监测更多的信息,更方便地沟通,并承担更广泛的责任,从而受益于技术进步。新技术将如何影响高技能和低技能工人的工资? 对于这个问题,分析供求变化如何影响市场(引入供求关系)的四步进程以这种方式发挥作用:

p82.original: Step 1. What did the markets for low-skill labor and high-skill labor look like before the arrival of the new technologies? In  (a) and  (b), S0 is the original supply curve for labor and D0 is the original demand curve for labor in each market. In each graph, the original point of equilibrium, E0, occurs at the price W0 and the quantity Q0.
p82.zh: 步骤1。 在新技术出现之前,低技能劳动力和高技能劳动力的市场是什么样子的? 在(a)和(b)中,S0是劳动力的原始供应曲线,D0是每个市场劳动力的原始需求曲线. 在每一个图中,原始的平衡点E0以W0和数量Q0的价格发生.

p83.original: Technology and Wages: Applying Demand and Supply
p83.zh: 技术和工资:应用需求和供应

p84.original: Step 2. Does the new technology affect the supply of labor from households or the demand for labor from firms? The technology change described here affects demand for labor by firms that hire workers.
p84.zh: 步骤二.新技术是否影响家庭劳动力的供应或企业对劳动力的需求?本文所述的技术变革影响到雇用工人的公司对劳动力的需求。

p85.original: Step 3. Will the new technology increase or decrease demand? Based on the description earlier, as the substitute for low-skill labor becomes available, demand for low-skill labor will shift to the left, from D0 to D1. As the technology complement for high-skill labor becomes cheaper, demand for high-skill labor will shift to the right, from D0 to D1.
p85.zh: 步骤3。新技术是否会增加或减少需求? 根据先前的描述,随着低技能劳动力的替代物的出现,对低技能劳动力的需求将转向左侧,从D0转向D1. 随着高技能劳动力的技术补充变得便宜,对高技能劳动力的需求将从D0转向D1。

p86.original: Step 4. The new equilibrium for low-skill labor, shown as point E1 with price W1 and quantity Q1, has a lower wage and quantity hired than the original equilibrium, E0. The new equilibrium for high-skill labor, shown as point E1 with price W1 and quantity Q1, has a higher wage and quantity hired than the original equilibrium (E0).
p86.zh: 步骤4。低技能劳动力的新平衡,与价格W1和数量Q1的E1点相比,工资和雇用的数量低于原先的平衡E0。高技能劳动力的新平衡与价格W1和数量Q1为E1点,其工资和雇用数量高于原先的平衡(E0)。

p87.original: Thus, the demand and supply model predicts that the new computer and communications technologies will raise the pay of high-skill workers but reduce the pay of low-skill workers. From the 1970s to the mid-2000s, the wage gap widened between high-skill and low-skill labor. According to the National Center for Education Statistics, in 1980, for example, a college graduate earned about 30% more than a high school graduate with comparable job experience, but by 2019, a college graduate earned about 59% more than an otherwise comparable high school graduate. Many economists believe that the trend toward greater wage inequality across the U.S. economy is due to improvements in technology.
p87.zh: 因此,供需模式预测,新的计算机和通信技术将提高高技能工人的工资,但降低低技能工人的工资。 从1970年代到2000年代中期,高技能劳动力和低技能劳动力之间的工资差距扩大。 据国家教育统计中心统计,比如1980年,大学毕业生的收入比具有可比工作经验的高中毕业生多30%左右,但到2019年,大学毕业生的收入比原本可比的高中毕业生多59%左右. 许多经济学家认为,整个美国经济工资不平等加剧的趋势是由于技术的改进.

p89.original: Price Floors in the Labor Market: Living Wages and Minimum Wages
p89.zh: 劳动力市场的价格下限:生活工资和最低工资

p90.original: In contrast to goods and services markets, price ceilings are rare in labor markets, because rules that prevent people from earning income are not politically popular. There is one exception: boards of trustees or stockholders, as an example, propose limits on the high incomes of top business executives.
p90.zh: 与商品和服务市场不同,劳动力市场中价格上限很少,因为阻碍人们赚取收入的规则在政治上并不普遍。 有一个例外:例如,董事会或股东会提议对高级企业经理的高收入加以限制。

p91.original: The labor market, however, presents some prominent examples of price floors, which are an attempt to increase the wages of low-paid workers. The U.S. government sets a minimum wage, a price floor that makes it illegal for an employer to pay employees less than a certain hourly rate. In mid-2009, the U.S. minimum wage was raised to $7.25 per hour. Local political movements in a number of U.S. cities have pushed for a higher minimum wage, which they call a living wage. Promoters of living wage laws maintain that the minimum wage is too low to ensure a reasonable standard of living. They base this conclusion on the calculation that, if you work 40 hours a week at a minimum wage of $7.25 per hour for 50 weeks a year, your annual income is $14,500, which is less than the official U.S. government definition of what it means for a family to be in poverty. (A family with two adults earning minimum wage and two young children will find it more cost efficient for one parent to provide childcare while the other works for income. Thus the family income would be $14,500, which is significantly lower than the federal poverty line for a family of four, which was $26,500 in 2021.)
p91.zh: 然而,劳动力市场提供了一些价格下限的突出例子,这是为提高低收入工人工资所作的努力。美国政府设定了最低工资标准,这一价格下限使得雇主支付低于一定小时工资标准的雇员是非法的.2009年年中,美国最低工资提高到每小时7.25美元. 一些美国城市的地方政治运动推动提高最低工资,他们称之为生活工资.生活工资法的提倡者认为,最低工资太低,无法确保合理的生活水平。 他们将这一结论建立在以下计算的基础上:如果您每周工作40小时,最低工资为每小时7.25美元,每年工作50周,那么您的年收入为14,500美元,这比美国政府官方对一个家庭陷入贫困意味着什么的定义要少.(一个家庭,有两个成年人挣到最低工资,两个年幼的子女,父母一方提供托儿服务,而另一人则从事赚取收入的工作,将更符合成本效益。) 因此,家庭收入为14 500美元,大大低于联邦对四口家庭的贫困线,2021年时为26 500美元。 )

p92.original: Supporters of the living wage argue that full-time workers should be assured a high enough wage so that they can afford the essentials of life: food, clothing, shelter, and healthcare. Since Baltimore passed the first living wage law in 1994, several dozen cities enacted similar laws in the late 1990s and the 2000s. The living wage ordinances do not apply to all employers, but they have specified that all employees of the city or employees of firms that the city hires be paid at least a certain wage that is usually a few dollars per hour above the U.S. minimum wage.
p92.zh: 生活工资的支持者认为,应当确保全职工人获得足够的工资,以便他们能够支付生活必需品:食物、衣服、住所和保健。 自1994年巴尔的摩通过第一部生活工资法以来,数十个城市在1990年代末和2000年代颁布了类似的法律.生活工资法令并不适用于所有雇主,但规定该市所有雇员或该市雇用的公司雇员至少应领取一定的工资,通常每小时比美国最低工资高几美元.

p93.original: illustrates the situation of a city considering a living wage law. For simplicity, we assume that there is no federal minimum wage. The wage appears on the vertical axis, because the wage is the price in the labor market. Before the passage of the living wage law, the equilibrium wage is $10 per hour and the city hires 1,200 workers at this wage. However, a group of concerned citizens persuades the city council to enact a living wage law requiring employers to pay no less than $12 per hour. In response to the higher wage, 1,600 workers look for jobs with the city. At this higher wage, the city, as an employer, is willing to hire only 700 workers. At the price floor, the quantity supplied exceeds the quantity demanded, and a surplus of labor exists in this market. For workers who continue to have a job at a higher salary, life has improved. For those who were willing to work at the old wage rate but lost their jobs with the wage increase, life has not improved.  shows the differences in supply and demand at different wages.
p93.zh: 说明一个城市考虑制定活工资法的情况。简而言之,我们假设没有联邦最低工资。工资出现在垂直轴上,因为工资是劳动力市场上的价格。生活工资法通过前,均衡工资为每小时10元,城市按该工资雇用1200名工人. 然而,一些有关的公民劝说市议会颁布一项生活工资法,要求雇主支付不少于每小时12美元的工资。 针对工资较高的情况,1600名工人随城市寻找工作.如此高的工资,城市作为一个雇主,只愿意雇用700名工人. 在价格下限,供应的数量超过要求的数量,在这个市场上存在劳动力过剩。 对于继续从事高薪工作的工人,生活有所改善。对于那些愿意按旧工资率工作但因工资增加而失去工作的人来说,生活没有改善。 这表明了不同工资的供求差异。

p94.original: A Living Wage: Example of a Price Floor
p94.zh: 生活工资:价格底线实例

p95.original: Living Wage: Example of a Price Floor
p95.zh: 生活工资:价格下限实例

p120.original: The Minimum Wage as an Example of a Price Floor
p120.zh: 最低工资作为价格下限的示例

p121.original: The U.S. minimum wage is a price floor that is set either very close to the equilibrium wage or even slightly below it. About 1.5% of hourly workers in the U.S. are paid the minimum wage. In other words, the vast majority of the U.S. labor force has its wages determined in the labor market, not as a result of the government price floor. However, for workers with low skills and little experience, like those without a high school diploma or teenagers, the minimum wage is quite important. In many cities, the federal minimum wage is apparently below the market price for unskilled labor, because employers offer more than the minimum wage to checkout clerks and other low-skill workers without any government prodding.
p121.zh: 美国的最低工资是一种价格下限,它要么非常接近平衡工资,要么甚至略低于平衡工资。 美国约1.5%的小时工人领取最低工资.换句话说,绝大多数美国劳动力的工资都由劳动力市场决定,而不是由于政府的价格下限. 然而,对于技能低和经验少的工人,如那些没有高中文凭或青少年的工人,最低工资相当重要。在许多城市,联邦最低工资显然低于非熟练劳动力的市场价格,因为雇主为离职办事员和其他低技能工人提供比最低工资更多的工资,而政府则不予任何拖延。

p122.original: Economists have attempted to estimate how much the minimum wage reduces the quantity demanded of low-skill labor. A typical result of such studies is that a 10% increase in the minimum wage would decrease the hiring of unskilled workers by 1 to 2%, which seems a relatively small reduction. In fact, some studies have even found no effect of a higher minimum wage on employment at certain times and places—although these studies are controversial. Well-known economists Walter Williams and Thomas Sowell, who both focus on the intersections of race and economics, argue that minimum wages increase discrimination and limit economic mobility. Williams, for example, indicates that higher minimum wages would increase employment barriers for lower-skilled workers, reducing the opportunity for them to learn on the job and gain experience that would give them more choice in employment.
p122.zh: 经济学家试图估计最低工资在多大程度上减少了低技能劳动力的需求。此类研究的一个典型结果是,最低工资增加10%将使雇用非技术工人的人数减少1%至2%,这似乎是一个较小的减少。 事实上,有些研究甚至发现,在某些时间和地点,提高最低工资对就业没有影响,尽管这些研究有争议。知名经济学家沃尔特·威廉姆斯和托马斯·索威尔都关注种族与经济学的交汇点,他们认为最低工资会增加歧视,限制经济流动性. 例如,威廉姆斯指出,提高最低工资将增加低技能工人的就业障碍,减少他们学习工作的机会,并获得经验,使他们在就业方面有更多的选择。

p123.original: Let’s suppose that the minimum wage lies just slightly below  the equilibrium wage level. Wages could fluctuate according to market forces above this price floor, but they would not be allowed to move beneath the floor. In this situation, the price floor minimum wage is nonbinding —that is, the price floor is not determining the market outcome. Even if the minimum wage moves just a little higher, it will still have no effect on the quantity of employment in the economy, as long as it remains below the equilibrium wage. Even if the government increases the minimum wage by enough so that it rises slightly above the equilibrium wage and becomes binding, there will be only a small excess supply gap between the quantity demanded and quantity supplied.
p123.zh: 让我们假设最低工资略低于平衡工资水平。工资可能因市场力量而波动,高于这一价格下限,但不允许在下限下流动。 在这种情况下,最低物价工资没有约束力,即最低物价不能决定市场结果。 即使最低工资稍高一点,只要低于平衡工资,它仍不会对经济中的就业数量产生影响。 即使政府提高最低工资,使其略高于平衡工资,并具有约束力,在所需数量和供应数量之间也只会出现少量的超额供应差距。

p124.original: These insights help to explain why U.S. minimum wage laws have historically had only a small impact on employment. Since the minimum wage has typically been set close to the equilibrium wage for low-skill labor and sometimes even below it, it has not had a large effect in creating an excess supply of labor. However, if the minimum wage increased dramatically—say, if it doubled to match the living wages that some U.S. cities have considered—then its impact on reducing the quantity demanded of employment would be far greater. The following Clear It Up feature describes in greater detail some of the arguments for and against changes to the minimum wage.
p124.zh: 这些见解有助于解释为什么美国最低工资法在历史上对就业只产生很小的影响. 由于最低工资通常与低技能劳动力的平衡工资接近,有时甚至低于平衡工资,因此在造成劳动力过剩供应方面没有产生很大影响。 然而,如果最低工资大幅增长,比如说,如果最低工资翻一番,与一些美国城市考虑的维持生计工资相匹配,那么最低工资对减少就业需求的影响就会大得多。 以下的“Clear Up”特征更详细地描述了一些支持和反对修改最低工资的论点。

p125.original: What’s the harm in raising the minimum wage?
p125.zh: 提高最低工资有何危害?

p126.original: Because of the law of demand, a higher required wage will reduce the amount of low-skill employment either in terms of employees or in terms of work hours. Although there is controversy over the numbers, let’s say for the sake of the argument that a 10% rise in the minimum wage will reduce the employment of low-skill workers by 2%. Does this outcome mean that raising the minimum wage by 10% is bad public policy? Not necessarily.
p126.zh: 由于需求法则,更高的所需工资将减少低技能就业,无论是从雇员还是从工作时间来看。以降低低技能工人的就业率为例, 将最低工资提高10%, 这一结果是否意味着将最低工资提高10%是不良的公共政策?不一定,我需要你帮忙 No maybe.

p127.original: If 98% of those receiving the minimum wage have a pay increase of 10%, but 2% of those receiving the minimum wage lose their jobs, are the gains for society as a whole greater than the losses? The answer is not clear, because job losses, even for a small group, may cause more pain than modest income gains for others. For one thing, we need to consider which minimum wage workers are losing their jobs. If the 2% of minimum wage workers who lose their jobs are struggling to support families, that is one thing. If those who lose their job are high school students picking up spending money over summer vacation, that is something else.
p127.zh: 如果98%的最低工资领取者的工资增加10%,但2%的最低工资领取者失业,那么整个社会的收益是否大于损失?答案并不明确,因为即使对一个小群体来说,失业也可能比对其他人微薄的收入收益造成更多的痛苦。 首先,我们需要考虑的是,哪些最低工资工人正在失去工作。 如果有2%的最低工资工人失业,他们却在挣扎养家糊口,这就是一回事。 如果那些失去工作的人是高中生 暑假拿钱,这是另外一回事。

p128.original: Another complexity is that many minimum wage workers do not work full-time for an entire year. Imagine a minimum wage worker who holds different part-time jobs for a few months at a time, with bouts of unemployment in between. The worker in this situation receives the 10% raise in the minimum wage when working, but also ends up working 2% fewer hours during the year because the higher minimum wage reduces how much employers want people to work. Overall, this worker’s income would rise because the 10% pay raise would more than offset the 2% fewer hours worked.
p128.zh: 另一复杂之处是,许多最低工资工人一整年不全职工作。想象一下,最低工资工人每次从事不同的兼职工作几个月,失业人数在两者之间激增。 在这种情况下,工人在工作时的最低工资增加10%,但一年中工作时数减少2%,因为较高的最低工资减少了雇主希望人们工作的程度。总体而言,这名工人的收入将会增加,因为10%的加薪将超过减少工作时间的2%。

p129.original: Of course, these arguments do not prove that raising the minimum wage is necessarily a good idea either. There may well be other, better public policy options for helping low-wage workers. (The Poverty and Economic Inequality chapter discusses some possibilities.) The lesson from this maze of minimum wage arguments is that complex social problems rarely have simple answers. Even those who agree on how a proposed economic policy affects quantity demanded and quantity supplied may still disagree on whether the policy is a good idea.
p129.zh: 当然,这些论点并不能证明提高最低工资也必然是一个好主意。 在帮助低工资工人方面,很可能还有其他更好的公共政策选择。(《贫穷和经济不平等》一章讨论了一些可能性。 )从最低工资论点的迷宫中吸取的教训是,复杂的社会问题很少有简单的答案。即使是那些同意拟议的经济政策如何影响所要求数量和所供应数量的人,也可能对这项政策是否是一个好主意仍有分歧。

p131.original: In the labor market, households are on the supply side of the market and firms are on the demand side. In the market for financial capital, households and firms can be on either side of the market: they are suppliers of financial capital when they save or make financial investments, and demanders of financial capital when they borrow or receive financial investments.
p131.zh: 在劳动力市场上,家庭处于市场供应方,企业处于需求方。 在金融资本市场中,家庭和公司可以站在市场两边:在储蓄或进行金融投资时,它们都是金融资本的提供者;在借贷或接受金融投资时,它们也是金融资本的需求者。

p132.original: In the demand and supply analysis of labor markets, we can measure the price by the annual salary or hourly wage received. We can measure the quantity of labor various ways, like number of workers or the number of hours worked.
p132.zh: 在劳动力市场的供需分析中,我们可以以年薪或每小时工资来衡量价格。 我们可以以各种方式衡量劳动力的数量,例如工人人数或工作时间。

p133.original: Factors that can shift the demand curve for labor include: a change in the quantity demanded of the product that the labor produces; a change in the production process that uses more or less labor; and a change in government policy that affects the quantity of labor that firms wish to hire at a given wage. Demand can also increase or decrease (shift) in response to: workers’ level of education and training, technology, the number of companies, and availability and price of other inputs.
p133.zh: 能够改变劳动力需求曲线的因素包括:劳动力生产的产品需求数量发生变化;生产过程或多或少使用劳动力;政府政策发生变化,影响企业希望按一定工资雇用的劳动力数量。需求也可能因下列因素而增加或减少(转移):工人的教育和培训水平、技术、公司数量、其他投入的提供和价格。

p134.original: The main factors that can shift the supply curve for labor are: how desirable a job appears to workers relative to the alternatives, government policy that either restricts or encourages the quantity of workers trained for the job, the number of workers in the economy, and required education.
p134.zh: 能够改变劳动力供给曲线的主要因素是:相对于替代方案而言,工人对工作是否可取,政府的政策是限制或鼓励接受过工作培训的工人数量、经济中的工人人数以及需要的教育。

p136.original: In the labor market, what causes a movement along the demand curve? What causes a shift in the demand curve?
p136.zh: 在劳动力市场上,是什么原因导致需求曲线移动的?是什么导致需求曲线变化的?

p137.original: Changes in the wage rate (the price of labor) cause a movement along the demand curve. A change in anything else that affects demand for labor (e.g., changes in output, changes in the production process that use more or less labor, government regulation) causes a shift in the demand curve.
p137.zh: 工资率(劳动力价格)的变化导致需求曲线上的变化。影响劳动力需求的其他任何变化(如产出变化,使用多少劳动力的生产过程变化,政府监管)都会导致需求曲线的转变.

p138.original: In the labor market, what causes a movement along the supply curve? What causes a shift in the supply curve?
p138.zh: 在劳动力市场上,是什么导致沿着供应曲线移动的?是什么导致供应曲线的转变?

p139.original: Changes in the wage rate (the price of labor) cause a movement along the supply curve. A change in anything else that affects supply of labor (e.g., changes in how desirable the job is perceived to be, government policy to promote training in the field) causes a shift in the supply curve.
p139.zh: 工资率(劳动力价格)的变化导致供应曲线沿线的变动。影响劳动力供应的其他任何变化(例如,对工作理想程度的改变、政府促进实地培训的政策)都会导致供应曲线的转变。

p140.original: Why is a living wage considered a price floor? Does imposing a living wage have the same outcome as a minimum wage?
p140.zh: 为什么生活工资被认为是最低价格?强制实行生活工资是否与最低工资产生同样的结果?

p141.original: Since a living wage is a suggested minimum wage, it acts like a price floor (assuming, of course, that it is followed). If the living wage is binding, it will cause an excess supply of labor at that wage rate.
p141.zh: 由于生活工资是建议的最低工资,它的作用就像一个价格下限(当然假定它得到遵守)。 如果生活工资具有约束力,将导致以该工资率提供过多的劳动力。

p143.original: What is the “price” commonly called in the labor market?
p143.zh: 劳动力市场上通常所谓的“价格”是什么?

p144.original: Are households demanders or suppliers in the goods market? Are firms demanders or suppliers in the goods market? What about the labor market and the financial market?
p144.zh: 商品市场是家庭需求者还是供应商?公司是商品市场的需求者还是供应商?劳动力市场和金融市场如何?

p145.zh: 列举一些可能导致劳动力市场需求曲线转变的因素。

p148.zh: 除了对劳动力的需求之外,什么是“衍生需求”的另一个例子?

p149.original: Suppose that a 5% increase in the minimum wage causes a 5% reduction in employment. How would this affect employers and how would it affect workers? In your opinion, would this be a good policy?
p149.zh: 假设最低工资提高5%会导致就业减少5%。 这会对雇主产生怎样的影响,对工人会产生怎样的影响? 你认为这是个好政策吗?

p150.original: Under what circumstances would a minimum wage be a nonbinding price floor? Under what circumstances would a living wage be a binding price floor?
p150.zh: 最低工资在什么情况下是无约束力的价格下限?生活工资在什么情况下是有约束力的最低价格?

p167.original: Demand and Supply in Financial Markets
p167.zh: 金融市场的需求和供应

p168.original: United States' households, institutions, and domestic businesses saved almost $1.3 trillion in 2015. Where did that savings go and how was it used? Some of the savings ended up in banks, which in turn loaned the money to individuals or businesses that wanted to borrow money. Some was invested in private companies or loaned to government agencies that wanted to borrow money to raise funds for purposes like building roads or mass transit. Some firms reinvested their savings in their own businesses.
p168.zh: 2015年,美国的家庭,机构和国内企业节省了近1.3万亿美元.储蓄去了哪里,如何使用?部分储蓄最终投靠银行,银行又将这笔钱借给想借钱的个人或企业. 有些投资是在私营公司投资,或借给政府机构,这些机构想借钱筹集资金,用于修建道路或大众运输。 一些公司将储蓄重新投资于自己的企业。

p169.original: In this section, we will determine how the demand and supply model links those who wish to supply financial capital (i.e., savings) with those who demand financial capital (i.e., borrowing). Those who save money (or make financial investments, which is the same thing), whether individuals or businesses, are on the supply side of the financial market. Those who borrow money are on the demand side of the financial market. For a more detailed treatment of the different kinds of financial investments like bank accounts, stocks and bonds, see the Financial Markets chapter.
p169.zh: 在本节中,我们将确定供求模式如何将希望提供金融资本(即储蓄)的人与需要金融资本(即借贷)的人联系起来。储蓄资金(或进行金融投资,这是同一件事)的人,无论是个人还是企业,都站在金融市场的供应方. 那些借钱的人是金融市场的需求方。 关于银行账户、股票和债券等不同类型的金融投资的更详细处理,见金融市场一章。

p170.original: Who Demands and Who Supplies in Financial Markets?
p170.zh: 金融市场中谁要求谁供应?

p171.original: In any market, the price is what suppliers receive and what demanders pay. In financial markets, those who supply financial capital through saving expect to receive a rate of return, while those who demand financial capital by receiving funds expect to pay a rate of return. This rate of return can come in a variety of forms, depending on the type of investment.
p171.zh: 在任何市场,价格都是供应商得到的,是需求者付出的。 在金融市场,通过储蓄提供金融资本的人预期会得到回报率,而通过接受资金而要求获得金融资本的人预期会得到回报率。 这种收益率可以有多种形式,取决于投资类型。

p172.original: The simplest example of a rate of return is the interest rate. For example, when you supply money into a savings account at a bank, you receive interest on your deposit. The interest the bank pays you as a percent of your deposits is the interest rate. Similarly, if you demand a loan to buy a car or a computer, you will need to pay interest on the money you borrow.
p172.zh: 回报率最简单的例子就是利率. 例如,向银行储蓄账户提供货币时,可收取存款利息。银行付给你的利息占你存款的百分之一 是利率 同样,如果您要求贷款购买汽车或计算机,您需要支付所借资金的利息。

p173.original: Let’s consider the market for borrowing money with credit cards. In 2021, almost 200 million Americans were cardholders. Credit cards allow you to borrow money from the card's issuer, and pay back the borrowed amount plus interest, although most allow you a period of time in which you can repay the loan without paying interest. A typical credit card interest rate ranges from 12% to 18% per year. In May 2021, Americans had about $807 billion outstanding in credit card debts. As of 2021, just over 45% of American families carried some credit card debt. Let’s say that, on average, the annual interest rate for credit card borrowing is 15% per year. Thus, Americans pay tens of billions of dollars every year in interest on their credit cards—plus basic fees for the credit card or fees for late payments.
p173.zh: 让我们考虑借信用卡借钱的市场。2021年,近2亿美国人持卡.信用卡允许您向卡的发行人借钱,并还清借款金额加利息,虽然大多数允许您有一段时间可以偿还贷款而无需支付利息.典型的信用卡利率从每年12%到18%不等.2021年5月,美国人的信用卡债务约有8,07亿美元未偿. 截至2021年,略高于45%的美国家庭背负了一些信用卡债务.举个例子,信用卡借款的年利率平均为每年15%。 因此,美国人每年支付数百亿美元的信用卡利息——加上信用卡的基本费用或迟付费用。

p174.original: illustrates demand and supply in the financial market for credit cards. The horizontal axis of the financial market shows the quantity of money loaned or borrowed in this market. The vertical or price axis shows the rate of return, which in the case of credit card borrowing we can measure with an interest rate.  shows the quantity of financial capital that consumers demand at various interest rates and the quantity that credit card firms (often banks) are willing to supply.
p174.zh: 说明金融市场对信用卡的供求情况。金融市场的横向轴线显示在这个市场上借出或借出的资金数量。纵向或价格轴显示回报率,在信用卡借款的情况下,我们可以以利率衡量。 显示消费者以各种利率要求的金融资本数量以及信用卡公司(通常为银行)愿意提供的数量。

p175.original: Demand and Supply for Borrowing Money with Credit Cards
p175.zh: 用信用卡借钱的需求和供应

p176.original: Demand and Supply for Borrowing Money with Credit Cards
p176.zh: 用信用卡借钱的需求和供应

p178.original: Quantity of Financial Capital Demanded (Borrowing) ($ billions)
p178.zh: 所需金融资本数量(10亿美元)

p179.original: Quantity of Financial Capital Supplied (Lending) ($ billions)
p179.zh: 金融资本供应量(10亿美元)

p198.original: The laws of demand and supply continue to apply in the financial markets. According to the law of demand, a higher rate of return (that is, a higher price) will decrease the quantity demanded. As the interest rate rises, consumers will reduce the quantity that they borrow. According to the law of supply, a higher price increases the quantity supplied. Consequently, as the interest rate paid on credit card borrowing rises, more firms will be eager to issue credit cards and to encourage customers to use them. Conversely, if the interest rate on credit cards falls, the quantity of financial capital supplied in the credit card market will decrease and the quantity demanded will increase.
p198.zh: 供求法继续适用于金融市场。 根据需求法,较高的回报率(即较高的价格)将减少所要求的数量。 随着利率的上升,消费者将减少借贷数量. 根据供应法,较高的价格会增加供应的数量。 因此,随着信用卡借款利率的上升,更多的公司将渴望发行信用卡并鼓励客户使用信用卡。 相反,如果信用卡利率下降,信用卡市场提供的金融资本数量将下降,所需数量将增加。

p200.original: In the financial market for credit cards in , the supply curve (S) and the demand curve (D) cross at the equilibrium point (E). The equilibrium occurs at an interest rate of 15%, where the quantity of funds demanded and the quantity supplied are equal at an equilibrium quantity of $600 billion.
p200.zh: 在 的信用卡金融市场中,供应曲线(S)和需求曲线(D)在平衡点(E)交叉.平衡以15%的利率进行,所需资金的数量和供应的数量相等于6 000亿美元的平衡数量。

p201.original: If the interest rate (remember, this measures the “price” in the financial market) is above the equilibrium level, then an excess supply, or a surplus, of financial capital will arise in this market. For example, at an interest rate of 21%, the quantity of funds supplied increases to $750 billion, while the quantity demanded decreases to $480 billion. At this above-equilibrium interest rate, firms are eager to supply loans to credit card borrowers, but relatively few people or businesses wish to borrow. As a result, some credit card firms will lower the interest rates (or other fees) they charge to attract more business. This strategy will push the interest rate down toward the equilibrium level.
p201.zh: 如果利率(记住,这一计量金融市场的“价格”)高于平衡水平,那么,这一市场将出现金融资本的过剩供应或盈余。 例如,按21%的利率,所提供资金的数量增加到7 500亿美元,而要求的数量则减少到4 800亿美元。 在这种高于平衡利率的情况下,公司急于向信用卡借款人提供贷款,但希望借款的人或企业相对较少. 因此,一些信用卡公司将降低其收取的利率(或其他费用),以吸引更多的业务。 这一战略将促使利率降低到平衡水平。

p202.original: If the interest rate is below the equilibrium, then excess demand or a shortage of funds occurs in this market. At an interest rate of 13%, the quantity of funds credit card borrowers demand increases to $700 billion, but the quantity credit card firms are willing to supply is only $510 billion. In this situation, credit card firms will perceive that they are overloaded with eager borrowers and conclude that they have an opportunity to raise interest rates or fees. The interest rate will face economic pressures to creep up toward the equilibrium level.
p202.zh: 如果利率低于平衡,则在这个市场出现超额需求或资金短缺。以13%的利率计算,信用卡借款人要求的资金数量增至7000亿美元,但信用卡公司愿意提供的数量仅为5100亿美元. 在这种情况下,信用卡公司会发现它们已经超负荷地挤压着渴望的借款人,并得出结论,它们有机会提高利率或提高费用.利率将面临经济压力,需要逐步达到平衡水平。

p203.original: The FRED database publishes some two dozen measures of interest rates, including interest rates on credit cards, automobile loans, personal loans, mortgage loans, and more. You can find these at the FRED website.
p203.zh: FRED数据库公布了大约20多种利率计量,包括信用卡利率,汽车贷款,个人贷款,抵押贷款等. 你可以在FRED网站上找到这些.

p204.original: Shifts in Demand and Supply in Financial Markets
p204.zh: 金融市场需求和供应的转移

p205.original: Those who supply financial capital face two broad decisions: how much to save, and how to divide up their savings among different forms of financial investments. We will discuss each of these in turn.
p205.zh: 提供金融资本的人面临两个广泛的决定:储蓄多少,如何将其储蓄分成不同形式的金融投资。 我们将依次讨论每个问题。

p206.original: Participants in financial markets must decide when they prefer to consume goods: now or in the future. Economists call this intertemporal decision making because it involves decisions across time. Unlike a decision about what to buy from the grocery store, people make investment or savings decisions across a period of time, sometimes a long period.
p206.zh: 金融市场的参与者必须决定他们选择何时消费货物:现在还是将来。经济学家称这种时际决策是因为它涉及跨时际的决策.与关于从杂货店购买什么的决定不同,人们在一段时间内做出投资或储蓄决定,有时是很长一段时间.

p207.original: Most workers save for retirement because their income in the present is greater than their needs, while the opposite will be true once they retire. Thus, they save today and supply financial markets. If their income increases, they save more. If their perceived situation in the future changes, they change the amount of their saving. For example, there is some evidence that Social Security, the program that workers pay into in order to qualify for government checks after retirement, has tended to reduce the quantity of financial capital that workers save. If this is true, Social Security has shifted the supply of financial capital at any interest rate to the left.
p207.zh: 大多数工人为退休而储蓄,因为他们目前的收入高于他们的需要,而一旦退休,情况就会相反。 因此,它们拯救了今天,为金融市场提供了供应。 如果他们的收入增加,他们就会节省更多。 如果它们将来的感知情况发生变化,它们就会改变其节省的金额。 例如,有证据表明,社会保障这一工人为获得退休后接受政府检查的资格而支付的方案,往往会减少工人节省的资金。 如果情况属实,社会保障将金融资本的供应以任何利率转移到左翼。

p208.original: By contrast, many college students need money today when their income is low (or nonexistent) to pay their college expenses. As a result, they borrow today and demand from financial markets. Once they graduate and become employed, they will pay back the loans. Individuals borrow money to purchase homes or cars. A business seeks financial investment so that it has the funds to build a factory or invest in a research and development project that will not pay off for five years, ten years, or even more. Thus, when consumers and businesses have greater confidence that they will be able to repay in the future, the quantity demanded of financial capital at any given interest rate will shift to the right.
p208.zh: 相比之下,许多大学生在收入低(或根本不存在)时,今天需要钱来支付他们的大学费用. 因此,它们今天从金融市场借款和需求。 一旦他们毕业并就业,他们将偿还贷款。个人借钱购买房屋或汽车. 一个企业寻求财政投资,以便拥有建设工厂或投资研发项目的资金,而研发项目五年、十年甚至更长的时间都得不到回报。 因此,当消费者和企业更加相信它们将来能够偿还债务时,按任何特定利率要求的金融资本数量将转移到右翼。

p209.original: For example, in the technology boom of the late 1990s, many businesses became extremely confident that investments in new technology would have a high rate of return, and their demand for financial capital shifted to the right. Conversely, during the 2008 and 2009 Great Recession, their demand for financial capital at any given interest rate shifted to the left.
p209.zh: 例如,在1990年代后期的技术繁荣中,许多企业对新技术投资的回报率很高,对金融资本的需求转移到了右翼。 相反,在2008年和2009年大衰退期间,他们以任何利率对金融资本的需求都转向了左翼。

p210.original: To this point, we have been looking at saving in total. Now let us consider what affects saving in different types of financial investments. In deciding between different forms of financial investments, suppliers of financial capital will have to consider the rates of return and the risks involved. Rate of return is a positive attribute of investments, but risk is a negative. If Investment A becomes more risky, or the return diminishes, then savers will shift their funds to Investment B—and the supply curve of financial capital for Investment A will shift back to the left while the supply curve of capital for Investment B shifts to the right.
p210.zh: 至此,我们一直在考虑总共节省资金。 现在,让我们考虑影响不同类型金融投资储蓄的因素。 在决定不同形式的金融投资时,金融资本供应商必须考虑收益率和所涉风险。收益率是投资的一个积极属性,但风险是负的。 如果投资A的风险增加,或者回报减少,储蓄者就会将资金转移到投资B上 — — 而投资A的金融资本供应曲线会向左转,而投资B的资本供应曲线则向右转。

p211.original: The United States as a Global Borrower

p212.original: In the global economy, trillions of dollars of financial investment cross national borders every year. In the early 2000s, financial investors from foreign countries were investing several hundred billion dollars per year more in the U.S. economy than U.S. financial investors were investing abroad. The following Work It Out deals with one of the macroeconomic concerns for the U.S. economy in recent years.
p212.zh: 在全球经济中,每年有数以万亿计的金融投资跨越国界。2000年代初,外国金融投资者每年在美国经济中的投资额比美国金融投资者在国外的投资额多几千亿美元. 以下的Work It Out涉及近年来美国经济的宏观经济问题之一.

p213.original: The Effect of Growing U.S. Debt

p214.original: Imagine that foreign investors viewed the U.S. economy as a less desirable place to put their money because of fears about the growth of the U.S. public debt. Using the four-step process for analyzing how changes in supply and demand affect equilibrium outcomes, how would increased U.S. public debt affect the equilibrium price and quantity for capital in U.S. financial markets?
p214.zh: 想象一下,由于担心美国公债的增长,外国投资者将美国经济视为放钱的不理想之地.利用四步进程分析供求变化如何影响均衡结果,美国公共债务的增加如何影响美国金融市场资本的均衡价格和数量?

p215.original: Step 1. Draw a diagram showing demand and supply for financial capital that represents the original scenario in which foreign investors are pouring money into the U.S. economy.  shows a demand curve, D, and a supply curve, S, where the supply of capital includes the funds arriving from foreign investors. The original equilibrium E0 occurs at interest rate R0 and quantity of financial investment Q0.
p215.zh: 步骤1。绘制一张显示金融资本需求和供应的图表,说明外国投资者向美国经济注入资金的最初情景。 该图表显示需求曲线D和供应曲线S,其中资本供应包括外国投资者到来的资金。最初的平衡E0发生于利率R0和金融投资数量Q0.

p216.original: The United States as a Global Borrower Before U.S. Debt Uncertainty
p216.zh: 美国作为全球借款人在美国之前.债务的不确定性

p217.original: Step 2. Will the diminished confidence in the U.S. economy as a place to invest affect demand or supply of financial capital? Yes, it will affect supply. Many foreign investors look to the U.S. financial markets to store their money in safe financial vehicles with low risk and stable returns. Diminished confidence means U.S. financial assets will be seen as more risky.
p217.zh: 步骤二. 对美国经济作为投资场所的信心下降是否会影响金融资本的供求? 是的,它会影响供应。 许多外国投资者期待美国金融市场将资金存放在风险低且回报稳定的安全金融工具中.信心下降意味着美国金融资产将被视为风险更大.

p218.original: Step 3. Will supply increase or decrease? When the enthusiasm of foreign investors’ for investing their money in the U.S. economy diminishes, the supply of financial capital shifts to the left.  shows the supply curve shift from S0 to S1.
p218.zh: 步骤3。供应会增加还是减少? 当外国投资者对美国经济投资的热情减弱时,金融资本的供应就转向了左翼。 这表明供应曲线从S0转向S1。

p219.original: The United States as a Global Borrower Before and After U.S. Debt Uncertainty
p219.zh: 美国作为美国前后的全球借款国.债务的不确定性

p220.original: Step 4. Thus, foreign investors’ diminished enthusiasm leads to a new equilibrium, E1, which occurs at the higher interest rate, R1, and the lower quantity of financial investment, Q1.  In short, U.S. borrowers will have to pay more interest on their borrowing.
p220.zh: 步骤4。 因此,外国投资者的热情下降导致新的平衡,即E1, 利率较高,R1, 金融投资数量较低, 问题1。简言之,美国借款人必须支付更多的借款利息.

p221.original: The economy has experienced an enormous inflow of foreign capital. According to the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, by the third quarter of 2021, U.S. investors had accumulated $34.45 trillion of foreign assets, but foreign investors owned a total of $50.53 trillion of U.S. assets. If foreign investors were to pull their money out of the U.S. economy and invest elsewhere in the world, the result could be a significantly lower quantity of financial investment in the United States, available only at a higher interest rate. This reduced inflow of foreign financial investment could impose hardship on U.S. consumers and firms interested in borrowing.
p221.zh: 经济经历了外国资本的大量流入。 据美国记载.经济分析局,截至2021年第三季度,美国投资者累计外资34.45万亿元,但外国投资者拥有美国总资产50.53万亿元. 如果外国投资者要将自己的钱从美国经济中抽出,并在世界其他地方投资,结果可能是在美国的金融投资数量会大大降低,只能以更高的利率获得.外国金融投资流入的减少可能给美国消费者和有意借贷的公司带来困难。

p222.original: In a modern, developed economy, financial capital often moves invisibly through electronic transfers between one bank account and another. Yet we can analyze these flows of funds with the same tools of demand and supply as markets for goods or labor.
p222.zh: 在现代发达经济体中,金融资本往往通过银行账户与银行账户之间的电子转账而隐形移动。 然而,我们可以分析这些资金流动,其供求手段与商品或劳务市场相同。

p223.original: Price Ceilings in Financial Markets: Usury Laws
p223.zh: 金融市场的价格上限:高利贷法

p224.original: As we noted earlier, about 200 million Americans own credit cards, and their interest payments and fees total tens of billions of dollars each year. It is little wonder that political pressures sometimes arise for setting limits on the interest rates or fees that credit card companies charge. The firms that issue credit cards, including banks, oil companies, phone companies, and retail stores, respond that the higher interest rates are necessary to cover the losses created by those who borrow on their credit cards and who do not repay on time or at all. These companies also point out that cardholders can avoid paying interest if they pay their bills on time.
p224.zh: 正如我们早些时候指出的,大约2亿美国人拥有信用卡,他们每年的利息支付和收费总额达数百亿美元.不足为奇的是,有时会出现对信用卡公司收取的利率或费用加以限制的政治压力。发放信用卡的公司,包括银行、石油公司、电话公司和零售商店,答复说,必须提高利率,以弥补那些借信用卡而根本不按时或完全偿还贷款的人所造成的损失。 这些公司还指出,持卡人如果按时支付账单,可以避免支付利息.

p225.original: Consider the credit card market as  illustrates. In this financial market, the vertical axis shows the interest rate (which is the price in the financial market). Demanders in the credit card market are households and businesses. Suppliers are the companies that issue credit cards. This figure does not use specific numbers, which would be hypothetical in any case, but instead focuses on the underlying economic relationships. Imagine a law imposes a price ceiling that holds the interest rate charged on credit cards at the rate Rc, which lies below the interest rate R0 that would otherwise have prevailed in the market. The horizontal dashed line at interest rate Rc in  shows the price ceiling. The demand and supply model predicts that at the lower price ceiling interest rate, the quantity demanded of credit card debt will increase from its original level of Q0 to Qd; however, the quantity supplied of credit card debt will decrease from the original Q0 to Qs. At the price ceiling (Rc), quantity demanded will exceed quantity supplied. Consequently, a number of people who want to have credit cards and are willing to pay the prevailing interest rate will find that companies are unwilling to issue cards to them. The result will be a credit shortage.
p225.zh: 将信用卡市场视为例证。 在这个金融市场中,纵向轴线显示利率(即金融市场的价格).信用卡市场的需求者是家庭和企业.供应商是发放信用卡的公司。这一数字并不使用具体数字,而只是假设数字,而是侧重于基本的经济关系。想象一下,法律规定了最高价格,将信用卡的利率维持在Rc,低于市场本来会占上风的利率R0。以利率Rc表示的横向虚线显示最高价格。供需模式预测,在价格上限较低的利率下,要求的信用卡债务数量将从原来的Q0级增加到Qd级;然而,提供信用卡债务的数量将从原来的Q0级减少到Qd级. 在最高价格(Rc)下,所需数量将超过供应数量。 因此,一些希望有信用卡并愿意支付现行利率的人会发现,公司不愿意向他们发放卡片。其结果将是信贷短缺。

p226.original: Credit Card Interest Rates: Another Price Ceiling Example
p226.zh: 信用卡利率:另一个价格上限示例

p227.original: Many states do have usury laws, which impose an upper limit on the interest rate that lenders can charge. However, in many cases these upper limits are well above the market interest rate. For example, if the interest rate is not allowed to rise above 30% per year, it can still fluctuate below that level according to market forces. A price ceiling that is set at a relatively high level is nonbinding, and it will have no practical effect unless the equilibrium price soars high enough to exceed the price ceiling.
p227.zh: 许多州确实有高利贷法,对放款人可以收取的利率规定了上限. 然而,在许多情况下,这些上限远远高于市场利率。 例如,如果不允许利率每年上升30%以上,则仍可以根据市场力量,在该水平以下浮动。设定在较高水平的价格上限是没有约束力的,除非平衡价格飞涨到足以超过最高价格,否则不会产生实际效果。

p229.original: In the demand and supply analysis of financial markets, the “price” is the rate of return or the interest rate received. We measure the quantity by the money that flows from those who supply financial capital to those who demand it.
p229.zh: 在金融市场的供求分析中,“价格”是收益率或收到的利率。 我们用那些提供金融资本的人向那些需要资金的人提供的资金来衡量资金的数量。

p230.original: Two factors can shift the supply of financial capital to a certain investment: if people want to alter their existing levels of consumption, and if the riskiness or return on one investment changes relative to other investments. Factors that can shift demand for capital include business confidence and consumer confidence in the future—since financial investments received in the present are typically repaid in the future.
p230.zh: 有两个因素可以将金融资本的供应转移到某种投资上:如果人们想改变他们现有的消费水平,以及如果一项投资的风险或回报相对于其他投资有所变化。改变对资本需求的因素包括企业信心和消费者对未来的信心,因为目前收到的金融投资通常在未来得到偿还。

p232.original: In the financial market, what causes a movement along the demand curve? What causes a shift in the demand curve?
p232.zh: 在金融市场上,是什么导致了需求曲线的移动?是什么导致需求曲线变化的?

p233.original: Changes in the interest rate (i.e., the price of financial capital) cause a movement along the demand curve. A change in anything else (non-price variable) that affects demand for financial capital (e.g., changes in confidence about the future, changes in needs for borrowing) would shift the demand curve.
p233.zh: 利率的变化(即金融资本的价格)导致需求曲线上的变化。影响金融资本需求的其他任何变化(非价格变量)(例如对未来信心的变化、借款需求的变化)都会改变需求曲线。

p234.original: In the financial market, what causes a movement along the supply curve? What causes a shift in the supply curve?
p234.zh: 在金融市场上,是什么导致沿着供应曲线移动的?是什么导致供应曲线的转变?

p235.original: Changes in the interest rate (i.e., the price of financial capital) cause a movement along the supply curve. A change in anything else that affects the supply of financial capital (a non-price variable) such as income or future needs would shift the supply curve.
p235.zh: 利率(即金融资本价格)的变动导致供应曲线沿线的变动。影响金融资本供应(非价格变量)的任何其它变化,如收入或未来需求,都会改变供应曲线。

p236.original: If a usury law limits interest rates to no more than 35%, what would the likely impact be on the amount of loans made and interest rates paid?
p236.zh: 如果高利贷法将利率限制在不超过35%的范围内,那么对贷款数额和支付的利率可能有什么影响?

p237.original: If market interest rates stay in their normal range, an interest rate limit of 35% would not be binding. If the equilibrium interest rate rose above 35%, the interest rate would be capped at that rate, and the quantity of loans would be lower than the equilibrium quantity, causing a shortage of loans.
p237.zh: 如果市场利率保持在正常范围内,35%的利率限制将不具有约束力。 如果平衡利率高于35%,利率将按该利率上限,贷款数量将低于平衡数量,导致贷款短缺。

p238.original: Which of the following changes in the financial market will lead to a decline in interest rates:
p238.zh: 金融市场的下列变化中,有哪一种会导致利率下降:

p243.original: b and c will lead to a fall in interest rates. At a lower demand, lenders will not be able to charge as much, and with more available lenders, competition for borrowers will drive rates down.
p243.zh: b和c将导致利率下降。 在需求降低的情况下,贷款人将无法收取那么多费用,如果贷款人更多,对借款人的竞争将降低利率。

p244.original: Which of the following changes in the financial market will lead to an increase in the quantity of loans made and received:
p244.zh: 金融市场的下列变化中,哪些会导致贷款和收到的贷款数量的增加:

p251.zh: 经济学家如何界定金融市场的平衡?

p252.zh: 金融市场短缺的征兆是什么?

p253.zh: 高利贷法是否有助于或妨碍解决金融市场的短缺?

p255.original: Suppose the U.S. economy began to grow more rapidly than other countries in the world. What would be the likely impact on U.S. financial markets as part of the global economy?
p255.zh: 假设美国经济开始比世界其他国家增长得更快. 作为全球经济的一部分,美国金融市场可能受到什么影响?

p256.zh: 如果政府规定所有贷款的联邦利率上限为20%,谁能赢,谁会输?

p258.zh: 预测下列经济变化将如何影响住房贷款金融市场的平衡价格和数量。绘制一个供求图来支持您的答案 。

p290.original: The Market System as an Efficient Mechanism for Information
p290.zh: 市场系统作为高效率的信息机制

p291.original: Prices exist in markets for goods and services, for labor, and for financial capital. In all of these markets, prices serve as a remarkable social mechanism for collecting, combining, and transmitting information that is relevant to the market—namely, the relationship between demand and supply—and then serving as messengers to convey that information to buyers and sellers. In a market-oriented economy, no government agency or guiding intelligence oversees the set of responses and interconnections that result from a change in price. Instead, each consumer reacts according to that person’s preferences and budget set, and each profit-seeking producer reacts to the impact on its expected profits. The following Clear It Up feature examines the demand and supply models.
p291.zh: 商品和服务市场、劳动力市场和金融资本市场都有价格。 在所有这些市场上,价格是收集、合并和传递与市场有关的信息(即供求关系)的显著社会机制,然后充当信使,向买方和卖方传达这一信息。 在市场经济中,没有任何政府机构或指导情报部门监督价格变动所产生的整套反应和相互联系。 相反,每个消费者都根据他们的偏好和预算来反应,每个追求利润的生产者都对其预期利润的影响作出反应。 以下的Clear It Up功能研究了供求模式.

p292.original: Why are demand and supply curves important?
p292.zh: 为什么需求和供应曲线很重要?

p293.original: The demand and supply model is the second fundamental diagram for this course. (The opportunity set model that we introduced in the Choice in a World of Scarcity chapter was the first.) Just as it would be foolish to try to learn the arithmetic of long division by memorizing every possible combination of numbers that can be divided by each other, it would be foolish to try to memorize every specific example of demand and supply in this chapter, this textbook, or this course. Demand and supply is not primarily a list of examples. It is a model to analyze prices and quantities. Even though demand and supply diagrams have many labels, they are fundamentally the same in their logic. Your goal should be to understand the underlying model so you can use it to analyze any market.
p293.zh: 供需模式是本课程的第二个基本图表。(我们在《在恐惧的世界中的选择》一章中引入的机会设定模式是第一个。 )正如试图通过对可以互相划分的每一个可能的数字组合进行记忆来学习长期分裂的算术一样,试图在本章、本教科书或本课程中记住每个具体的供求例子是愚蠢的。需求和供应主要不是一个例子。这是一种分析价格和数量的模式。 尽管供需图有许多标签,但它们的逻辑基本相同. 你的目标应该是了解基本模型 这样你就可以用它来分析任何市场

p294.original: displays a generic demand and supply curve. The horizontal axis shows the different measures of quantity: a quantity of a good or service, or a quantity of labor for a given job, or a quantity of financial capital. The vertical axis shows a measure of price: the price of a good or service, the wage in the labor market, or the rate of return (like the interest rate) in the financial market.
p294.zh: 显示通用供求曲线。横向轴线显示不同数量尺度:货物或服务的数量,或特定工作的劳动力的数量,或金融资本的数量。纵向轴线显示价格的尺度:货物或服务的价格、劳动力市场的工资或金融市场的收益率(如利率)。

p295.original: The demand and supply model can explain the existing levels of prices, wages, and rates of return. To carry out such an analysis, think about the quantity that will be demanded at each price and the quantity that will be supplied at each price—that is, think about the shape of the demand and supply curves—and how these forces will combine to produce equilibrium.
p295.zh: 供求模式可以解释现有的价格、工资和回报率水平。 为了进行这种分析,考虑按每一价格要求的数量和按每一价格提供的数量,即考虑供求曲线的形状,以及这些力量如何结合起来产生平衡。

p296.original: We can also use demand and supply to explain how economic events will cause changes in prices, wages, and rates of return. There are only four possibilities: the change in any single event may cause the demand curve to shift right or to shift left, or it may cause the supply curve to shift right or to shift left. The key to analyzing the effect of an economic event on equilibrium prices and quantities is to determine which of these four possibilities occurred. The way to do this correctly is to think back to the list of factors that shift the demand and supply curves. Note that if more than one variable is changing at the same time, the overall impact will depend on the degree of the shifts. When there are multiple variables, economists isolate each change and analyze it independently.
p296.zh: 我们还可以利用供求来解释经济事件将如何导致价格、工资和收益率的变化。仅有四种可能性: 任何单一事件的变化都可能导致需求曲线向右转向或向左转向,或者可能导致供应曲线向右转向或向左转向.分析经济事件对均衡价格和数量的影响的关键是确定这四种可能性中有哪些发生。正确做到这一点的方法是回想一下改变供求曲线的因素清单.请注意,如果一个以上的变量同时在变化,整体影响将取决于变化的程度. 当有多个变量时,经济学家将每个变化隔离,独立分析.

p298.original: An increase in the price of some product signals consumers that there is a shortage; therefore, they may want to economize on buying this product. For example, if you are thinking about taking a plane trip to Hawaii, but the ticket turns out to be expensive during the week you intend to go, you might consider other weeks when the ticket might be cheaper. The price could be high because you were planning to travel during a holiday when demand for traveling is high. Maybe the cost of an input like jet fuel increased or the airline has raised the price temporarily to see how many people are willing to pay it. Perhaps all of these factors are present at the same time. You do not need to analyze the market and break down the price change into its underlying factors. You just have to look at the ticket price and decide whether and when to fly.
p298.zh: 一些产品价格的上涨向消费者表明存在短缺;因此,他们可能想在购买这种产品时节省开支。 例如,如果你在考虑去夏威夷旅行, 但事实证明,在你打算去的一周里,机票价格很贵, 你可能会考虑其他几周的机票可能更便宜。价格可能很高,因为你计划旅行 在旅行需求高的假日。 也许像喷气燃料这样的投入成本会增加,或者航空公司暂时提高了价格,看看有多少人愿意支付. 也许所有这些因素同时存在。 你不需要分析市场,将价格变化细分为其根本因素。 你只需要看看票价,决定是否和何时飞.

p299.original: In the same way, price changes provide useful information to producers. Imagine the situation of a farmer who grows oats and learns that the price of oats has risen. The higher price could be due to an increase in demand caused by a new scientific study proclaiming that eating oats is especially healthful. Perhaps the price of a substitute grain, like corn, has risen, and people have responded by buying more oats. The oat farmer does not need to know the details. The farmer only needs to know that the price of oats has risen and that it will be profitable to expand production as a result.
p299.zh: 同样,价格变化为生产者提供了有用的信息。想象一个种植燕麦的农民的情况,得知燕麦的价格已经上涨.价格较高可能是由于一项新的科学研究宣布食用燕麦特别健康,导致需求增加。 也许替代谷物的价格,像玉米一样,已经上涨,人们通过购买更多的燕麦来回应.燕麦农不需要知道细节.农民只需知道燕麦价格已经上涨,因此扩大生产是有利可图的.

p300.original: The actions of individual consumers and producers as they react to prices overlap and interlock in markets for goods, labor, and financial capital. A change in any single market is transmitted through these multiple interconnections to other markets. The vision of the role of flexible prices helping markets to reach equilibrium and linking different markets together helps to explain why price controls can be so counterproductive. Price controls are government laws that serve to regulate prices rather than allow the various markets to determine prices. There is an old proverb: “Don’t kill the messenger.” In ancient times, messengers carried information between distant cities and kingdoms. When they brought bad news, there was an emotional impulse to kill the messenger. However, killing the messenger did not kill the bad news. Moreover, killing the messenger had an undesirable side effect: Other messengers would refuse to bring news to that city or kingdom, depriving its citizens of vital information.
p300.zh: 个别消费者和生产者在对商品、劳动力和金融资本市场价格重叠和相互交错作出反应时所采取的行动。任何单一市场的变化都通过这些多重互联传递到其他市场。灵活价格有助于市场实现平衡和将不同市场联系起来,这种设想有助于解释为什么价格控制会起反作用。价格控制是政府的法律,用来规范价格,而不是让各个市场决定价格。古老的谚语是“不要杀死使者 ” 。 在古代,信使在遥远的城市和王国之间传递信息。 当他们带来坏消息时,有一种情绪冲动要杀死信使. 然而,杀死信使并没有杀死坏消息. 此外,杀害信使还会产生不良的副作用:其他信使会拒绝将消息带到该城市或王国,剥夺其公民的重要信息.

p301.original: Those who seek price controls are trying to kill the messenger—or at least to stifle an unwelcome message that prices are bringing about the equilibrium level of price and quantity. However, price controls do nothing to affect the underlying forces of demand and supply, and this can have serious repercussions. During China’s “Great Leap Forward” in the late 1950s, the government kept food prices artificially low, with the result that 30 to 40 million people died of starvation because the low prices depressed farm production. This was communist party leader Mao Zedong's social and economic campaign to rapidly transform the country from an agrarian economy to a socialist society through rapid industrialization and collectivization. Changes in demand and supply will continue to reveal themselves through consumers’ and producers’ behavior. Immobilizing the price messenger through price controls will deprive everyone in the economy of critical information. Without this information, it becomes difficult for everyone—buyers and sellers alike—to react in a flexible and appropriate manner as changes occur throughout the economy.
p301.zh: 那些寻求价格控制的人试图杀死信使——或者至少扼杀一个不受欢迎的信息,即价格正在带来价格和数量平衡的水平。 然而,价格控制对需求和供应的基本力量没有任何影响,这可能产生严重影响。 在20世纪50年代末的中国"大跃进"期间,政府人为维持低粮价,结果3000万至4000万人因低粮价压低了农业生产而饿死. 这是共产主义政党领袖毛泽东的社会和经济运动,通过迅速的工业化和集体化,使国家从农业经济迅速转变为社会主义社会.需求与供给的变化将继续通过消费者和生产者的行为显现出来。 通过价格控制动员价格信使,将使经济中的每个人都失去关键的信息. 如果没有这种资料,就很难在经济全过程中出现变化时,每个人——买方和卖方——都以灵活和适当的方式作出反应。

p309.original: The market price system provides a highly efficient mechanism for disseminating information about relative scarcities of goods, services, labor, and financial capital. Market participants do not need to know why prices have changed, only that the changes require them to revisit previous decisions they made about supply and demand. Price controls hide information about the true scarcity of products and thereby cause misallocation of resources.

At an above-equilibrium interest rate like 21%, the quantity of financial capital supplied would increase to $750 billion, but the quantity demanded would decrease to $480 billion. At a below-equilibrium interest rate like 13%, the quantity of financial capital demanded would increase to $700 billion, but the quantity of financial capital supplied would decrease to $510 billion.
c5.zh: 在这个信用卡借款的市场中,借款金融资本的需求曲线(D)在平衡E时交叉了贷款金融资本的供应曲线(S). 在均衡情况下,利率(这个市场的“价格”)为15%,贷款和借贷的金融资本数量为6 000亿美元。平衡价格是指所需数量和供应数量相等的地方。以21%的高于平衡利率计算,所供应的金融资本将增加到7 500亿美元,但所需数额将减少到4 800亿美元。以13%的低于平衡利率计算,所需金融资本的数量将增加到7 000亿美元,但所供应的金融资本的数量将减少到5 100亿美元。

c9.original: The original intersection of demand D and supply S occurs at equilibrium E0. However, a price ceiling is set at the interest rate Rc, below the equilibrium interest rate R0, and so the interest rate cannot adjust upward to the equilibrium. At the price ceiling, the quantity demanded, Qd, exceeds the quantity supplied, Qs. There is excess demand, also called a shortage.
c9.zh: 需求D和供应S的最初交汇点发生在E0平衡时. 然而,价格上限被设定为低于平衡利率R0的利率Rc,因此利率不能向上调整以适应平衡. 在最高价格,要求的数量,Qd,超过供应的数量,Qs.需求过剩,也称短缺。

c10.original: The figure displays a generic demand and supply curve. The horizontal axis shows the different measures of quantity: a quantity of a good or service, a quantity of labor for a given job, or a quantity of financial capital. The vertical axis shows a measure of price: the price of a good or service, the wage in the labor market, or the rate of return (like the interest rate) in the financial market. We can use the demand and supply curves explain how economic events will cause changes in prices, wages, and rates of return.
c10.zh: 这一数字显示了通用的供需曲线.横向轴线显示不同数量尺度:货物或服务的数量,特定工作的劳动力数量,或金融资本的数量。纵向轴线显示价格的尺度:货物或服务的价格、劳动力市场的工资或金融市场的收益率(如利率)。 我们可以使用供需曲线来解释经济事件将如何导致价格,工资,回报率的变化.

c11.original: In 2020, the median salary for nurses was $75,330. As demand for services increases, the demand curve shifts to the right (from D0 to D1) and the equilibrium quantity of nurses increases from Qe0 to Qe1. The equilibrium salary increases from Pe0 to Pe1.
c11.zh: 2020年,护士工资中位数为75,330. 随着对服务需求的增加,需求曲线向右转(从D0向D1),护士的均衡数量从Qe0向Qe1增加.平衡工资从Pe0增加到Pe1。

c12.original: The increase in demand for nurses shown in Figure 4.10 leads to both higher prices and higher quantities demanded. As nurses retire from the work force, the supply of nurses decreases, causing a leftward shift in the supply curve and higher salaries for nurses at Pe2. The net effect on the equilibrium quantity of nurses is uncertain, which in this representation is less than Qe1, but more than the initial Qe0.
c12.zh: 图4.10所示对护士的需求增加,导致价格上涨和需求增加。 随着护士从劳动力队伍中退休,护士供应减少,导致供应曲线左倾转变,Pe2的护士工资提高. 对护士均衡数量的净影响是不确定的,在这种表述中,护士数量小于Qe1,但多于最初的Qe0.
